questions.text: GlobalMart is upgrading its 15-year-old monolithic inventory system to a cloud-native, component-based architecture. Apply the principle of loose coupling to determine how they should integrate a new third-party shipping service.

options.text: Hard-code the third-party API calls directly into the core inventory logic.
Implement an interface-based adapter to mediate between the system and the service.
Merge the shipping service's source code into the main inventory database.
Use a single global variable to share data between the inventory and shipping modules.
Disable all security protocols to speed up the data transfer between systems.

questions.text: A developer at GlobalMart needs to fix a critical bug in the legacy payment module while other teams are restructuring the database. How should they use SCM branching to manage this?

options.text: Work directly on the main production branch to save time.
Create a dedicated bug-fix branch to isolate the change from the ongoing restructuring.
Wait for the database restructuring to finish before starting the bug fix.
Delete the existing payment module and rewrite it in the database branch.
Share their local files via email with the database team for manual merging.

questions.text: GlobalMart’s system is experiencing "Architecture Degradation" due to years of unplanned patches. Illustrate the best change-resistant strategy to prevent this in the new system.

options.text: Allow every developer to modify any part of the system architecture as needed.
Implement strict encapsulation to hide internal logic behind stable interfaces.
Remove all documentation to allow for faster, undocumented code changes.
Use a monolithic structure so that all code is in a single, visible file.
Avoid using any design patterns to keep the code as simple as possible.

questions.text: Apply the ISO/IEC 14764 standard to GlobalMart's plan to move its inventory data to the cloud. What is the first step in the "Migration" process?

options.text: Shut down the old system immediately to prevent data changes.
Develop a migration plan including requirement analysis and tool selection.
Delete the legacy database once the first 10% of data is moved.
Tell users the system will be unavailable for one month without notice.
Start writing the cloud code without analyzing the legacy data structure.

questions.text: GlobalMart discovers that a recent update caused the checkout process to fail for 20% of users. Use SCM "Rollback" techniques to solve this issue effectively.

options.text: Manually edit the production code until the errors stop appearing.
Revert the production environment to the last stable baseline recorded in Git.
Ask the affected users to re-install their web browsers.
Wait for the next scheduled update in three months to fix the issue.
Delete the checkout module and ask users to call the store to pay.

questions.text: To support "Controlled Evolution," GlobalMart wants to ensure that adding a "Loyalty Points" feature does not break existing sales reports. Which technique should they implement?

options.text: Static analysis of the user interface only.
Regression testing against a documented baseline after the new feature is added.
Manual code review of the sales report logic without running the system.
Increasing the server's RAM to handle the extra complexity.
Changing the sales report format to match the loyalty points data.

questions.text: GlobalMart is in the "Servicing Stage" of its legacy POS software. Use the staged model guidelines to determine the appropriate action for a request for a "Major Virtual Reality Shopping" feature.

options.text: Implement the feature immediately to stay ahead of competitors.
Reject the feature as it exceeds the scope of the servicing stage and suggest a new project.
Add the feature but do not test it to save maintenance resources.
Rewrite the entire POS system to include the VR feature as a patch.
Outsource the VR feature to a team that doesn't have access to the source code.

questions.text: A change request is submitted to modify the tax calculation logic in GlobalMart’s system. Apply "Impact Analysis" to decide if the change should proceed.

options.text: Approve the change immediately because tax laws are important.
Identify all modules that call the tax function and evaluate potential side effects.
Only check the tax module itself and ignore its connections to the checkout module.
Ask the developer who wrote the tax code 10 years ago for their opinion.
Implement the change in production and wait for user complaints to see the impact.

questions.text: GlobalMart wants to ensure that their re-engineered components are "Replaceable." Implement this design property for their database access layer.

options.text: Hard-code SQL queries for a specific database brand into every UI component.
Use a Data Access Object (DAO) pattern with a well-defined interface.
Store all database credentials in a plain text file on the developer's desktop.
Make the database layer dependent on the specific version of the operating system.
Encrypt the database layer so that no other component can communicate with it.

questions.text: Demonstrate how Lehman’s "Law of Increasing Complexity" should be handled during the evolution of GlobalMart’s inventory system.

options.text: Add as many features as possible without ever cleaning up the old code.
Schedule regular "Perfective Maintenance" phases to refactor and simplify the code.
Ignore the complexity until the system stops working entirely.
Fire developers who suggest that the system is becoming too complex.
Use more complex programming languages to match the system's complexity.

questions.text: GlobalMart’s legacy system has "Inconsistent Data Formats." Apply a data re-engineering strategy to prepare for migration to a modern SQL database.

options.text: Copy the data exactly as it is and fix errors manually in the new database later.
Use a data cleansing tool to standardize formats before the extraction process.
Delete any data that does not fit the new format to save storage space.
Change the new database schema to allow for every possible inconsistent format.
Use a manual spreadsheet to track the data instead of a database.

questions.text: Show how "Configuration Audit" should be used when GlobalMart hires a third-party team to restructure their shipping module.

options.text: Trust the third party completely and do not check their work.
Verify that the delivered code matches the approved change requests and standards.
Only check if the code runs on the lead developer's laptop.
Pay the third party based on the number of lines of code they wrote.
Ask the third party to write their own audit report and sign it.

questions.text: GlobalMart is transitioning a system to the "Phase-out Stage." Apply the appropriate maintenance strategy for this stage.

options.text: Hire 50 new developers to add revolutionary features.
Focus on migration planning and providing only critical security patches.
Stop all support immediately and turn off the servers without warning.
Re-brand the system as a new product to increase sales during the decline.
Move the source code to an open-source repository and walk away.

questions.text: Apply the concept of "Information Hiding" to GlobalMart's new inventory component.

options.text: Ensure that the inventory levels are visible to every other module in the system.
Hide the internal list structure and only provide "GetCount" and "UpdateLevel" methods.
Make the source code of the component available on the company's public website.
Use global variables so that any developer can change the inventory data directly.
Hide the documentation so that only the original author can understand the component.

questions.text: Solve a conflict where two developers at GlobalMart modified the same "Discount" function at the same time using SCM.

options.text: Use a version control merge tool to resolve conflicts and create a unified version.
Delete both developers' work and ask them to start over from the beginning.
Keep the version that was saved last and discard the other version.
Create two different versions of the software and let the users choose which one to use.
Ask the project manager to flip a coin to decide which version to keep.

questions.text: GlobalMart wants to reduce the risk of "Regression Errors" during a technology upgrade. Illustrate the most effective strategy.

options.text: Upgrade the hardware and the software at the same time without testing.
Use an SCM tool to create a baseline and run automated regression tests after each change.
Only test the parts of the system that are used by the CEO.
Tell the developers to be very careful not to make any mistakes.
Delete all old test cases and write new ones from scratch after the upgrade.

questions.text: Implement a "Change Control Board" (CCB) process for a request to change the GlobalMart employee login screen.

options.text: Allow the UI designer to make the change whenever they feel inspired.
Require the request to be documented, analyzed for impact, and approved by the CCB.
Let the employees vote on the login screen design on social media.
Change the login screen every day to keep the system feeling "fresh."
Ignore the request because the login screen is not a functional part of the system.

questions.text: Use the "Servicing Stage" characteristics to justify why GlobalMart should NOT perform a major database schema redesign on a 20-year-old HR system.

options.text: Because the database is too old to be redesigned.
Because the focus is on reliability and stability, not risky structural changes.
Because the original database designer has retired.
Because the company wants to spend the budget on a new marketing campaign.
Because the HR system is going to be deleted tomorrow anyway.

questions.text: Apply "Perfective Maintenance" to GlobalMart’s reporting module which is currently slow but accurate.

options.text: Fix a bug that causes the report to show the wrong date.
Refactor the SQL queries to improve the execution speed of the reports.
Update the reports to work on the latest version of the Chrome browser.
Add a new type of report for "Summer Sales" that wasn't there before.
Delete the reporting module and use a manual paper-based system.

questions.text: Demonstrate how "Encapsulation" supports the maintenance of GlobalMart’s "Price Calculation" component.

options.text: By allowing the component to access the private data of the "Customer" component.
By ensuring that changes to the internal math logic do not require changes in the UI components.
By making the component run in a virtual machine that is disconnected from the network.
By encrypting the pricing data so that even the database cannot read it.
By requiring the price calculation to be done manually by a manager.

questions.text: GlobalMart needs to move from an on-premise server to Azure. Apply the "Migration and Retirement" phase of ISO/IEC 14764.

options.text: Keep both systems running forever to ensure that no data is lost.
Plan the migration, execute it in stages, and formally retire the old system after validation.
Turn off the old server and hope that the new cloud system works immediately.
Only move the data that was created in the last 24 hours.
Ask the users to manually copy their data from the old system to the new one.

questions.text: Show how "Version Tracking" would help GlobalMart identify when a specific security vulnerability was introduced.

options.text: By looking at the physical date on the server's hard drive.
By reviewing the SCM commit history to see which change modified the vulnerable code.
By asking every developer if they remember writing a bug last month.
By checking the system's electricity usage over the last year.
By running a virus scan on the project manager's computer.

questions.text: GlobalMart wants to implement a "Change-Resistant" strategy for their external API integrations. Which approach should they use?

options.text: Use a "Wrapper" or "Facade" pattern to isolate external API changes from the internal system.
Connect the internal system directly to the external API's internal database.
Write the internal system in the same language as the external API to ensure compatibility.
Require the external API company to never change their code again.
Disable the API and use manual data entry to avoid any changes.

questions.text: Apply Lehman’s "Law of Continuing Change" to justify GlobalMart’s decision to update their mobile app every month.

options.text: Because the developers need to stay busy to justify their salaries.
Because the app must adapt to changing user needs and OS updates or it will become useless.
Because the law requires all apps to be updated at least 12 times a year.
Because frequent updates prevent the app from taking up too much memory.
Because users like to see the "Update" button in the app store.

questions.text: Implement "Corrective Maintenance" on GlobalMart’s "Search" feature which currently crashes when a user enters a special character.

options.text: Add a new feature that allows users to search by voice.
Modify the code to handle special characters and prevent the system crash.
Change the background color of the search page to make it look better.
Update the search engine to work on the latest version of Linux.
Tell users not to use special characters in the search box.

questions.text: Use "Traceability" to support a change request for GlobalMart’s "Discount Module."

options.text: Trace the change request back to the original business requirement and forward to the affected code and tests.
Trace the physical location of the developer who is working on the discount module.
Trace the history of the discount module's name since the company was founded.
Trace the amount of money the company has saved by using the discount module.
Trace the electricity consumption of the discount module during peak hours.

questions.text: GlobalMart is using "IBM Rational ClearCase" for SCM. Illustrate a scenario where "Build Auditing" is applied.

options.text: Checking the office for any unauthorized hardware before a build.
Automatically recording which versions of which files were used to create a specific executable.
Counting the number of errors the compiler finds and charging the developer a fee.
Ensuring that the developer is sitting at their desk during the entire build process.
Verifying that the build server is using a licensed version of the operating system.

questions.text: Apply the "Staged Model" to explain why GlobalMart's "Initial Development" team should not be the same as the "Servicing" team.

options.text: Because the servicing team is not as smart as the initial development team.
Because the skills needed for rapid feature creation differ from those needed for long-term stability and bug fixing.
Because the company wants to save money by hiring cheaper developers for servicing.
Because the initial development team is required to go on vacation after the first release.
Because the servicing stage is handled by the marketing department.

questions.text: Demonstrate the use of "Adaptive Maintenance" for GlobalMart’s "Tax System" when a new VAT law is passed.

options.text: Fix a bug that was causing the tax system to crash on Sundays.
Update the tax calculation logic to comply with the new government regulations.
Improve the performance of the tax system so it can process 1,000 transactions per second.
Add a new user interface for the tax system that works on tablets.
Delete the tax system and use a flat-rate tax for every product.

questions.text: GlobalMart’s architecture is "Monolithic." Use re-engineering techniques to solve the problem of "High Deployment Risk."

options.text: Deploy the entire 10GB monolith every time a single word is changed on the website.
Refactor the monolith into independent microservices or components that can be deployed separately.
Only deploy the system at midnight when no one is using it.
Require five different managers to sign a paper before every deployment.
Stop making any changes to the system to avoid the risk of deployment.

questions.text: Apply the "Baseline" concept to GlobalMart's "Version 2.0" release.

options.text: The baseline is the lowest level of performance the system is allowed to have.
The baseline is a frozen set of code and documentation that represents the official state of Version 2.0.
The baseline is the list of developers who worked on Version 2.0.
The baseline is the total cost of developing Version 2.0.
The baseline is the first line of code written for Version 2.0.

questions.text: Show how "Component Reusability" should be applied when GlobalMart builds a new "Customer Loyalty" app.

options.text: Write all new code for the loyalty app to ensure it is modern.
Integrate the existing, tested "Authentication" and "Notification" components into the new app.
Copy the source code of the old app and change the name of the project.
Ask the developers to write the same functions in a different language to prove their skill.
Use the loyalty app to replace the main shopping app entirely.

questions.text: Implement a "Change Resistance" strategy for GlobalMart's legacy database schema that cannot be changed without breaking 50 other apps.

options.text: Change the database schema anyway and deal with the 50 broken apps later.
Create a "Database View" or "API Layer" that provides the new data format while keeping the old tables for legacy apps.
Delete the 50 legacy apps and replace them with one new app.
Manually update the data in the database using a text editor every day.
Ask the database company to fix the schema for free.

questions.text: Use "Static Analysis" to evaluate the quality of a new module before it is integrated into GlobalMart's core system.

options.text: Run the module on a server and see if it crashes.
Use a tool to check the source code for complexity, style violations, and potential logic errors without running it.
Ask a user to try the module and see if they like the interface.
Compare the module's file size to the size of other modules in the system.
Print the source code and look at it from a distance to see if it looks organized.

questions.text: Apply the "Preventive Maintenance" strategy to GlobalMart's "Session Management" system.

options.text: Fix a bug that was logging users out randomly.
Update the system to use a more secure encryption algorithm before any hack occurs.
Add a new feature that shows the user's profile picture during the session.
Move the session management to a new server because the old one is dusty.
Delete the sessions after 5 minutes to save memory on the server.

questions.text: Demonstrate how "SCM Version Control" prevents "Lost Updates" in GlobalMart’s collaborative environment.

options.text: By only allowing one person to work on the entire project at a time.
By merging changes and alerting developers if they try to overwrite a newer version of a file.
By making the source code "read-only" for everyone except the lead developer.
By saving a new copy of every file with the developer's name at the end.
By requiring developers to write their code on paper before typing it into the computer.

questions.text: GlobalMart's "Inventory Component" has "Strong Coupling" with the "Pricing Component." Illustrate how to fix this for better maintainability.

options.text: Merge both components into one giant "InventoryAndPricing" component.
Introduce an event-based system or an interface so they communicate without knowing each other's internal details.
Delete the pricing component and let the inventory component handle prices.
Make the pricing component a sub-folder of the inventory component.
Require the inventory component to use the same database tables as the pricing component.

questions.text: Apply "IEEE 1219" to GlobalMart’s maintenance process. What should follow the "Implementation" phase?

options.text: The "Retirement" phase.
The "Review and Acceptance" phase, including testing and user approval.
The "Initial Development" phase.
The "Marketing and Sales" phase.
The "Developer Vacation" phase.

questions.text: Show how "Impact Analysis" would be used if GlobalMart decides to change the "Customer ID" from an integer to a string.

options.text: Change it in the database and see which programs stop working the next day.
Search the entire codebase and database schemas to find all references to "CustomerID" and assess the work needed.
Only change it in the UI and leave the database as an integer.
Tell the customers that their IDs have changed and they need to sign up again.
Ask the database administrator to change the ID type while the system is running.

questions.text: Implement "Configuration Control" for GlobalMart’s "Production Environment" settings.

options.text: Allow any IT staff member to change the server settings whenever they want.
Use a "Configuration Management" tool to track and approve all changes to environment variables.
Write the settings on a sticky note and put it on the side of the server.
Hard-code the production settings into the application's source code.
Use the same settings for "Testing" and "Production" to avoid any confusion.

questions.text: GlobalMart is moving to the "Evolution Stage" for its new "Grocery Delivery" app. Use the staged model to predict the team's main activity.

options.text: Fixing 1,000 bugs that were found in the first week.
Adding new features like "Real-time Tracking" and "Subscription Models" based on user feedback.
Planning the retirement of the app because grocery delivery is no longer popular.
Rewriting the app in a different language to make it faster.
Deleting the app's documentation to make it easier to change.

questions.text: Apply the "Encapsulation" principle to GlobalMart's "Credit Card Processing" module.

options.text: Ensure that the module exposes the raw encryption keys to the checkout module.
Hide the encryption logic and only provide a "ProcessPayment" method that returns success or failure.
Allow the "Order History" module to modify the credit card data directly in memory.
Store the credit card numbers in a public global variable for easy access.
Make the module's source code visible to every user who visits the website.

questions.text: Demonstrate the benefit of "Modular" design when GlobalMart's "Notification Component" crashes.

options.text: The entire website goes down and no one can buy anything.
Only the notifications stop working, while users can still browse and buy products.
The website automatically switches to a backup notification system made by a different company.
The website's background color changes to red to warn the users.
The "Inventory" component also crashes because it is waiting for a notification.

questions.text: GlobalMart wants to "Modernize" its legacy system without a "Big Bang" replacement. Apply the best strategy.

options.text: Replace the entire system on a single weekend and hope for the best.
Use "Incremental Re-engineering" to replace one module at a time using "Strangler Fig" pattern.
Stop all business for a year while the new system is being built.
Ask the developers to work 24 hours a day until the new system is finished.
Hire a new company to build a different system that has nothing to do with the old one.

questions.text: Use "Dynamic Analysis" to solve a "Memory Leak" problem in GlobalMart’s "Data Sync" service.

options.text: Read the source code carefully to find where the memory is not being released.
Run the service with a profiler tool to observe memory usage in real-time and identify the growing objects.
Increase the server's virtual memory until the service stops crashing.
Restart the service every hour to clear the leaked memory.
Delete the parts of the code that use the most memory.

questions.text: Apply the "Reusability" design property to GlobalMart’s "Address Validation" logic.

options.text: Write the address validation code separately for the web, mobile, and shipping modules.
Create a single "AddressService" component that all other modules call via an API.
Use a third-party address validator and pay for it every time it is called.
Ask the users to validate their own addresses using a map.
Only validate addresses for customers who spend more than $100.

questions.text: GlobalMart’s "Legacy Code" is "Difficult to Understand." Implement a "Program Understanding" strategy for a new developer.

options.text: Tell the developer to read all 1 million lines of code in the first week.
Provide the developer with visualization tools, call graphs, and high-level architectural diagrams.
Ask the developer to rewrite the entire system because the old code is too hard.
Give the developer a list of variable names and their meanings on a piece of paper.
Tell the developer to just start changing things and see what happens.

questions.text: Show how "Loose Coupling" would help GlobalMart if they decide to switch from "Azure" to "AWS."

options.text: They would have to rewrite every single line of code in the system.
Only the "Infrastructure Adaptation" layer would need to change, leaving the business logic untouched.
The system would automatically move itself to AWS because it is loosely coupled.
They would need to hire a completely different team of developers.
AWS would have to change its platform to match GlobalMart's code.

questions.text: Apply "SCM Baselines" to GlobalMart's "Sprint 5" development cycle.

options.text: The baseline is the amount of coffee the developers drink during the sprint.
The baseline is the approved state of the code at the end of Sprint 5, used as the start for Sprint 6.
The baseline is the total number of hours worked by the team in Sprint 5.
The baseline is the first bug found during the Sprint 5 testing phase.
The baseline is the lowest temperature in the server room during the sprint.

questions.text: Implement a "Change Request" process for an "Urgent Security Patch" at GlobalMart.

options.text: Bypass all change control and apply the patch to production immediately.
Use an "Emergency Change" procedure that allows for rapid approval followed by retrospective documentation.
Wait for the next monthly Change Control Board meeting to discuss the patch.
Tell the hackers that the system is being patched and they should stop.
Turn off the entire system until the patch is approved by the CEO.
